title: The close accepts a legal change and refuses a lone edit
requirement: REQ-294: confirmed board changes survive an interrupted write and the close does not let manual edits through. AC-3: after a legal row change the close refuses a lone edit of the row or of a whole journal event; a lagging export is not tampering; existing consistent records and old rows with the previous journal need no mass rewrite.
steps: Create a task, link a subagent and deliver its completion event, then close: the close must be accepted.
On a fresh board repeat the same path, change the row title by hand and close: refused with TASK_JOURNAL_MISMATCH.
On a fresh board repeat the same path, remove one whole event record of the row and close: refused with TASK_JOURNAL_MISMATCH.

On a fresh board move a task to review with a result, save the export, update the title, then put back the older export (a lagging export): the close must be accepted and the confirmed journal change read after reopening.
On a fresh board write a row with a consistent event in the previous journal layout and close it: accepted.
expected: The legal child-completion close is accepted; one hand-edited row is refused with TASK_JOURNAL_MISMATCH; a removed whole event record is refused with TASK_JOURNAL_MISMATCH; a lagging export is accepted and the confirmed journal change is read after reopening; an old consistent row with the previous journal layout closes.
failsWhen: The close takes a legitimate non-update change (a child completion) for a manual row edit and refuses it; after the change is stored in one record the close would also miss a hand-edited row or a deleted whole journal event.
trigger: A legal child-completion change is closed; then on fresh boards it is followed by one hand edit of the row, by removing one whole journal event, by a lagging export, and by an old consistent row with the previous journal.
oracle: REQ-294 and AC-3 in the analysis record taskboard-write-integrity: the close refuses a lone edit of the row or of a whole journal event, and old rows without a journal need no mass rewrite.
realism: The analysis business problem: a legitimate board change is taken for a manual edit; and the protection the fix must keep while it stores the change and its verification data in one record. The orchestrator confirmed the realism of the criteria.
